title: Inverse Plancherel transform tested against Schwartz functions
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure on $\mathbf R^m$, $m\geq1$. Let $L^2$ mean measurable square-integrable complex functions modulo almost-everywhere equality. Let $\mathcal S$ be the Schwartz class of smooth complex functions $\phi$ such that $\sup_x\|x\|^k\|D^n\phi(x)\|<\infty$ for all integers $k,n\geq0$. Write $\mathcal F_2$ for the continuous $L^2$ extension of $\mathcal F\phi(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\phi(x)\,dx$ on $\mathcal S$, and $\mathcal G_2$ for its inverse. Then $\mathcal G_2\mathcal F_2 u=u$ for every $u\in L^2$. For every $v\in L^2$, every measurable representative $v_0$ of $v$, every measurable representative $w_0$ of $\mathcal G_2v$, and every $\phi\in\mathcal S$, one has $$\int\phi(x)w_0(x)\,dx=\int (\mathcal G\phi)(\xi)v_0(\xi)\,d\xi,\qquad (\mathcal G\phi)(\xi)=\int e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\phi(x)\,dx.$$ Here the inverse transform on Schwartz functions is the displayed integral.
